reference_rationale: The recommended papers relate to each other and the query paper through their focus on improving cancer diagnosis and treatment by leveraging advanced computational methods and histopathology images. Paper [2] "Prediction of cancer treatment response from histopathology images through imputed transcriptomics" builds on the idea presented in paper [4] "hist2RNA: An Efficient Deep Learning Architecture to Predict Gene Expression from Breast Cancer Histopathology Images", as both use deep learning to predict genetic information from histopathology images. Paper [5] "Self-supervised attention-based deep learning for pan-cancer mutation prediction from histopathology" extends this concept by predicting genetic alterations from pathology slides, which can be used to identify cancer biomarkers. In contrast to paper [3] "Computational pathology improves risk stratification of a multi-gene assay for early stage ER+ breast cancer", which focuses on improving risk stratification using computational pathology, papers [2], [4], and [5] focus on predicting treatment response and genetic alterations from histopathology images. Paper [1] "Mutational signatures reveal mutual exclusivity of homologous recombination and mismatch repair deficiencies in colorectal and stomach tumors" uses a different approach, analyzing mutational signatures to investigate DNA damage and repair mechanisms, but its findings could potentially be used to inform the development of cancer biomarkers.

ground_truth_papers.abstract: A lack of well-trained clinical oncologists can result in significant cancer health disparities.
